summary:
Catalog transport-input revalidation in SDD 2.5.2 rereads captured SDK/runtime/template files through the operation's original custody. stableBytes allocated each payload-sized native buffer until final releaseKnown, while completed Task<CapturedFile> results also retained the reread managed arrays. Repeating unchanged validation therefore accumulated both domains, even though each read had completed.

The source repair at 40e44033 retires the synchronous read buffer inside its original registered IO worker, after its native use and managed copy have finished, under the original cleanup end. The caller never frees a buffer on await timeout. One-use pointer slots and uncertain cleanup remain owned. Revalidation projects exact byte/hash comparison to bool before completing the task, so no new captured payload survives in its result. It keeps the original custody and KnownFiles bindings: an identical-byte replacement inode still refuses. A fresh custody per reread must not silently adopt the replacement as a new first identity.

Five bounded small-file controls cover sixteen unchanged 256 KiB rereads, byte/hash mutation, identical-byte substitution, failed-read settlement and stopped-work cleanup. Separate causal variants restoring native retention or managed result retention fail their respective allocation/result assertions. These controls prove the accumulation mechanism, not the cause of the historical carrier OOM: the original failing allocation, pass count and memory peak were not observed. Full SDK capture/scaffold, a matching contained glibc 2.44 carrier, package publication and public consumer qualification remain separate gates.
title: Bound transport reread storage without resetting original custody
